question:
A chemical manufacturing process is modeled by the system:

$x + y + z = 6$
$2x + 3y + 2z = 15$
$4x + 7y + 5z = 32$

(a) Is the coefficient matrix singular? How does this affect the solution?
(b) Solve for $x, y, z$ using the matrix method and explain each step in terms of row operations and invertibility.
(c) Interpret your findings in the context of resource allocation in a chemical plant.
explanation:
(a) The coefficient matrix is
$A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 7 & 5\end{bmatrix}$
Let us find the determinant:
$|A| = 1\begin{vmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 7 & 5\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{vmatrix} + 1\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 7\end{vmatrix}$
$= 1(3\cdot5 - 2\cdot7) - 1(2\cdot5 - 2\cdot4) + 1(2\cdot7 - 3\cdot4)$
$= 1(15-14) - 1(10-8) + 1(14-12)$
$= 1(1) - 1(2) + 1(2) = 1 - 2 + 2 = 1$
Since $|A| = 1 \ne 0$, matrix $A$ is non-singular. A unique solution exists.

(b) System in matrix form:
$AX = B$ where $X = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}$, $B = \begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 15 \\ 32\end{bmatrix}$.
Compute $A^{-1}$:
Calculate the matrix of cofactors:
First row:
$A_{11} = +(3\cdot5 - 2\cdot7) = 15-14 = 1$
$A_{12} = -(2\cdot5-2\cdot4) = -(10-8) = -2$
$A_{13} = +(2\cdot7-3\cdot4) = 14-12=2$
Second row:
$A_{21} = -(1\cdot5-1\cdot7) = -(5-7)=2$
$A_{22} = +(1\cdot5-1\cdot4) = 5-4=1$
$A_{23} = -(1\cdot7-1\cdot4) = -(7-4)=-3$
Third row:
$A_{31} = +(1\cdot2-1\cdot3) = 2-3 = -1$
$A_{32} = -(1\cdot2-1\cdot2) = -(2-2)=0$
$A_{33} = +(1\cdot3-1\cdot2) = 3-2=1$
Cofactor matrix:
$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
Adjoint (transpose):
$\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\ -2&1&0\\ 2&-3&1\end{bmatrix}$
Thus,
$A^{-1} = \operatorname{adj}A / |A| = \operatorname{adj}A$
So,
$X = A^{-1}B = \begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\ -2&1&0\\ 2&-3&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}6\\15\\32\end{bmatrix}$
First row: $1\cdot6 + 2\cdot15 + -1\cdot32 = 6+30-32=4$
Second: $-2\cdot6 + 1\cdot15 + 0\cdot32 = -12+15=3$
Third: $2\cdot6 + (-3)\cdot15 + 1\cdot32 = 12-45+32 = -1$
$X = \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}$
So $x=4, y=3, z=-1$.

(c) Each variable corresponds to a type of resource, and the unique solution means each amount can be specifically allocated. The process can be precisely controlled and resources distributed without redundancy or ambiguity.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=0$, so the coefficient matrix is singular and the system has infinitely many solutions.
(b) The values are $x=4, y=3, z=-1$.
(c) The allocation is not unique, so many resource distributions are possible.
options.B:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the coefficient matrix is non-singular and the system has a unique solution.
(b) Using $X=A^{-1}B$, the solution is $x=4, y=3, z=-1$.
(c) The unique solution means each resource quantity is fixed, so the plant can allocate resources without ambiguity.
options.C:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the coefficient matrix is non-singular and the system has a unique solution.
(b) Using $X=A^{-1}B$, the solution is $x=-4, y=-3, z=1$.
(c) The negative values show the process is impossible and no allocation can be made.
options.D:
(a) $|A|=-1\ne0$, so the coefficient matrix is singular and the system has no solution.
(b) Since $A^{-1}$ does not exist, $x,y,z$ cannot be found.
(c) The chemical plant cannot determine any resource allocation.
